$comment: The highest-leverage text in the repo. Meshy's reconstruction quality is mostly a function of how clean the reference image is. The asset-list skill fills ONLY the {{description}} and {{materialNotes}} slots -- it must never hand-write this boilerplate, or 150 assets drift apart visually.

thai-street-photoreal-v1.label: Thai street, photoreal prop plate
thai-street-photoreal-v1.textureSuffix: Physically based materials. Surface detail must come from fine relief -- pitting, grain, weave, weld beads, scratches -- not from painted-on shading. No baked lighting, no baked ambient occlusion, no painted shadows in the base colour.
$notes: One image, not a four-view sheet. The turnaround bought a little reconstruction accuracy and cost a splitter, a rejection loop and a 50x more expensive image model; a single three-quarter plate is what Meshy's image-to-3d wants anyway.
50% grey backdrop, not white: white or bright props vanish into a white matte and Meshy's background separation eats them.
'no cast shadow / no ground plane' is repeated deliberately -- it is the most-ignored instruction, and baked contact shadows become permanent dark smears on the albedo.

The camera clause comes FIRST and shouts. A cheap fast model reads the opening line hardest: with the same clause buried after the object description, flux/schnell returned a flat straight-on elevation, which reconstructs as a slab. Moved to the top and made blunt, the same seed budget returns the top face. The three-quarter angle is what carries the depth cues when there is only one image.

The 'Form' paragraph is the cheapest poly-count control there is. A bottle crate drawn as a dense lattice of slots reconstructs as topology the simplifier cannot cut -- it stalled at 6002 triangles against a 2500 target even at a 0.05 error ceiling. Simplifying the object at the image stage costs a third of a cent; fighting it downstream costs a whole regeneration loop.

The Form paragraph must never contain the words 'low-poly' or 'low-polygon'. The prompt ends with 'not low-poly' for a reason -- a faceted render reconstructs badly and violates the kit's notLowPoly rubric axis. Constrain the object's SHAPE without handing the image model a style cue it will happily obey.

Contact shadows survive a whole paragraph of negations. Image models follow a positive description far more reliably than a list of prohibitions, so the backdrop clause STATES that the object floats with nothing beneath it, and keeps the negations as backup.

The 50% grey backdrop is asked for and often ignored -- a cheap model hands back a white product matte instead. That is fine and no longer worth fighting: prepare-image.mjs MEASURES the backdrop and pads with it, so the plate is consistent whatever colour arrives.
thai-street-photoreal-v1.image:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: {{description}} {{materialNotes}}

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.
